title: Agent Extensions Ecosystem — Launch Playbook and Roadmap
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical launch playbook and multi-quarter roadmap for the Agent Extensions Ecosystem (AEE) — a new commercial and technical product layer that enables third-party agent-like extensions (tooling, connectors, and workflows) to be discovered, deployed and billed alongside Redwood model consumption. The AEE complements Redwood Optimize and the Variant Marketplace by enabling structured tool integrations that run in a sandboxed, observable runtime surface.

Goals

- Deliver a secure, low-friction path for partners and customers to publish agent extensions that call external tools or run small functions during inference flows.
- Provide clear packaging and pricing so customers can consume curated agent extensions with predictable SLOs and costs.
- Ensure the runtime enforces isolation, observability, and rollback policies to preserve reliability and data residency requirements.

Scope and non-goals

- In scope: partner SDK, extension registry, runtime sandboxing (WASM-based), observability surface, billing hooks, canary rollout flow, basic security review checklist.
- Out of scope for Beta: on-prem distributed extension routing, HSM-level secret passing, complex multi-tenant extension chaining beyond one external call per token window.

Target customers and personas

- Developer platform teams embedding Redwood-driven assistants that need structured tool access (e.g., CRM connector, HR lookup, vector-store fetcher).
- ISV partners building reusable agent extensions to distribute to enterprise customers.
- Platform owners managing governance and cost for extension use.

Success metrics (90-day post-launch)

- Active extensions: >= 12 third-party extensions published in the registry.
- Customer adoption: >= 25 customers enabling at least one extension in production.
- Reliability: target extension execution success rate >= 99.2% (measured end-to-end).
- Cost model fit: median per-invocation billing parity within +/- 10% of forecasted unit cost.

SLOs and observability

- Extension invocation latency SLO: P95 <= 250ms per external call for compatible regions and P99 <= 600ms (Beta tolerances).
- End-to-end error budget: 0.8% monthly for extension invocation failures (distinct from model token SLOs).
- Traces: every extension invocation must emit a trace with correlation ids: request_id, extension_id, runtime_instance_id.
- Logs: structured invocation logs stored for 30 days by default, with customer-configurable retention.

Packaging and pricing (recommended Beta model)

We propose a two-part pricing model during Beta to keep billing predictable while enabling partner payouts:

1) Extension execution unit: per-invocation charge (fixed cents) based on extension class (light, medium, heavy).
2) Add-on model variant surcharge: when extension usage triggers a higher-fidelity model or reserved capacity, prorated model token uplift applies.

Suggested tiers (illustrative):

| Tier | Execution unit | Typical use case | Notes |
|------|----------------|------------------|-------|
| Light | $0.003 / invocation | stateless fetchers, single small HTTP call | <= 200ms expected response |
| Medium | $0.01 / invocation | plugins that run small compute, vector-store fetch | up to 500ms |
| Heavy | $0.05 / invocation | long-running integrations or chained external lookups | reserved or canary required |

Partner revenue share: 70/30 split during Beta; revisit for GA. Billing event schema will include: extension_id, partner_id, invocation_cost_cents, related_model_variant, timestamp.

Technical design summary

- Runtime: lightweight WASM-based sandbox (Runtime name: aee-runtime v0.1) loaded next to the serving process. Each invocation runs in an isolated worker with bounded CPU and memory.
- Compatibility: extensions must implement the AEE contract (JSON over STDIN/STDOUT) and declare external call scopes (outbound domains, secrets required).
- Security: secrets are provided via short-lived scoped tokens through Redwood secret manager and limited to declared domains. No persistent outgoing credentials.
- Observability: the runtime emits structured telemetry to the standard telemetry pipeline with an "aee." prefix. Sampling: 100% traces for errors, 1% for successful invocations in Beta.

Integration checklist (developer-facing)

1. Register extension metadata in the registry: manifest.yml including id, name, schema, allowed_domains, memory_limit, cpu_limit, signing_key.
2. Run compatibility test locally with the local-sandbox and redwood-invoke CLI. Example:

$ redwood-invoke --extension ./crm-lookup.wasm --payload '{"query":"customer_email"}' --timeout 2s

3. Submit partner onboarding form and sign the partner terms (for revenue share).
4. Submit security checklist and automated scanner report.

Runtime contract (example)

- Input JSON fields: request_id, tenant_id, user_context, params.
- Output JSON fields: status (ok|error), result, cost_hint_tokens (optional).

Example payload:

{
  "request_id": "req-6f2d3a",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_123",
  "user_context": {"locale": "en-US"},
  "params": {"email": "user@example.com"}
}

Governance and safety review

- Mandatory checks before public listing: domain allowlist verification, data exfiltration static analysis, runtime memory/cpu limits verified in staging.
- Privacy: extensions must declare PII handling; any extension that returns PII to Redwood logs must include a retention justification and map to customer-configurable retention.

Rollout phases and timeline (Q4 2026 — Q2 2027)

Phase 0 — Internal alpha (Oct 2026):
- Deliver basic runtime and registry, onboard 3 internal extensions (search connector, csv importer, mock-payments).
- Validate invocation tracing and billing event pipeline.

Phase 1 — Partner Beta (Nov 2026 — Feb 2027):
- Open partner SDK, invite 8-12 partners.
- Launch extension registry in private mode and implement partner revenue share flows.
- Metrics: reach 12 published extensions, 10 production-enabled customers.

Phase 2 — Public Beta (Mar 2027 — May 2027):
- Public listing, marketplace browsing, self-serve onboarding with basic automated checks.
- Introduce per-invocation pricing and dashboarding in Console.

Phase 3 — GA (target Jun 2027):
- Formalize SLAs, expand revenue share options and partner payout automation, introduce on-prem packaging.

Rollout playbook (canary steps)

1. Canary cohort: select 5 low-risk tenants (non-regulated) with traffic mirroring enabled.
2. Monitor P95 latency, error traces, unexpected outbound domains.
3. If error budget > 50% consumed in 24h, pause new enrollments and rollback to previous runtime image.

Customer console and UX notes

- Console additions: Extension Registry page (browse, install, enable/disable), per-extension telemetry tab, invocation budget controls, per-tenant allowlist.
- UX copy: clearly display execution unit cost and expected model variant uplift before enabling.

Go-to-market and enablement

- Sales enablement: one-pager for AE teams explaining partner margins, use-case playbooks (CRM enrichment, knowledge-base search, calendar actions).
- Developer docs: partner SDK quickstart, local sandbox guide, testing harness, CLI examples.
- Launch content: blog post, sample integrations repo, walkthrough video. Early PR focus: integrations that reduce customer latency or reduce token usage (e.g., vector store fetchers that avoid long prompt contexts).

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: uncontrolled outbound behavior by extensions causing data leakage. Mitigation: domain allowlists and static analysis, runtime egress filtering.
- Risk: billing complexity for customers. Mitigation: conservative default pricing, per-invocation caps, transparent cost breakdown in Console.
- Risk: partner fraud or low-quality extensions. Mitigation: staged discovery and partner verification; user ratings and rollback flows.

Ownership and runbooks

- Product owner: Sofia Martinez (product) — overall roadmap and partner program.
- Runtime & infra: Marco Nguyen (eng-serving-runtime) — sandbox runtime, autoscaling and isolation.
- Security review: Priya Desai (security) — gating for public listing.
- Console & billing: Anika Patel (eng-platform) — UI and billing pipeline integration.

Operational playbook (short)

1. If an extension causes a P95 latency spike > 2x baseline for an affected tenant: a) immediately mark extension as paused for that tenant, b) notify product owners and tenant admin, c) create SEV-1 if customer impact > 10% of calls.
2. For suspected data exfiltration: rotate tenant-facing short-lived secrets, quarantine logs, escalate to security, and suspend extension listing pending investigation.

Key beta release notes (what Beta includes)

- AEE runtime v0.1 with WASM sandboxing.
- Extension registry (private mode) and partner SDK.
- Billing event schema and basic Console visibility for executions.
- Canary rollout tooling and per-tenant allowlist controls.

Appendix A — API contract example

Minimal example of extension manifest (YAML):

---
id: "crm-lookup"
name: "CRM Lookup"
version: "0.1.0"
entrypoint: "main.wasm"
allowed_domains: ["api.crm.example.com"]
memory_limit: 64MB
cpu_limit: 0.25
scopes: ["read:contacts"]
billing_class: "light"
---

Questions and next steps

- Decision required: confirm Beta pricing tiers and partner revenue share agreement by 2026-11-15.
- Action: engineering to complete staging egress filters and secret passthrough demo by 2026-11-28.
- Product to prepare AE enablement and partner contract addendum before partner beta invites.

For comments, edits, or to volunteer a partner for early onboarding, please leave a note on this page or tag the author.
